agent.problem: Multiple choice dominates every stop: 7 of 9 choice cards in stop 1 and 5 of 7 in each of stops 2 and 3. Stops 2 and 3 also repeat the exact same question-type sequence: multiple choice, multiple choice, true/false, multiple choice, multiple choice, true/false, multiple choice.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

human.problem: 'Then that line again' points back to 'But my hand will never be against you.' The baker has never seen that line from verse 12. Card 9 cuts the quote off with an ellipsis before it, and card 10 only tests the idea as a true-or-false question. 'Again' assumes the baker read wording they were never shown.
human.question: Can a story card say a line is repeated ("that line again") when the first time that line appears was never shown to the baker, only tested indirectly on a choice card? Or must the first appearance be shown on a card first?

human.problem: Two wrong answers, "Takes Saul's spear" and "Takes Saul's water jug," are things David really does later in this same story group, in 1 Samuel 26:12. Stop 2 card 6 uses the same pair. When bakers reach that later passage, they will already have seen these marked as wrong. That could confuse them, or prime them on a later choice card.
human.question: Can wrong answers be real events from a later passage in the same story group? Or should they avoid details that a later lesson in the group will ask about?
